reading.body:
NTT CH3 sits on Pierce Road in Itasca, a suburb roughly 25 miles west of Chicago's core, and publishes 36 MW of IT capacity. Among the six Illinois facilities this site has read IT capacity figures from, that total reaches 236 MW, and CH3 ranks second by published megawatts, accounting for roughly 15 percent of that published figure. The other 38 mapped Illinois facilities publish no capacity number, so the state total visible here is a floor, not a census.

Thirty-six megawatts of IT load is a meaningful block of power for AI work. As an assumption, at 40 kW per rack, a density common in GPU-dense AI training deployments, 36 MW would support roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more conservative colocation average, the same power supports roughly 3,600 racks. The arithmetic is 36,000 kW divided by the assumed kilowatts per rack. NTT does not publish a per-rack density figure for this facility, so neither number is the operator's claim.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications for this campus, so no reading of certification scope is possible from the data. What the published record does establish is a facility large enough in absolute terms to host AI inference workloads or portions of a training cluster, positioned in a state where grid and land constraints have begun to slow new capacity, and ranked near the top of the limited Illinois capacity this site can currently quantify.
